VRF SYSTEM – PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
DAILY PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
A. GENERAL SYSTEM STATUS (All Units)
1 Check central controller (DCM 601 A51) display – verify no active fault/error codes present
2 Check individual room thermostats (BRC1H 81W) – verify no alarm indications on any zone
3 Verify VRF system is operating in the correct mode (Cooling / Heating / Fan Only)
4 Confirm all enabled indoor units are responding to setpoint and operating normally
5 Check outdoor unit LED/display panel (VRFU-1 & VRFU-2) for abnormal status indicators
B. INDOOR UNITS – CEILING CONCEALED (FXSQ 20A–125A | IU-01 to IU-26 applicable units)
6 Visual inspection – no visible water dripping from unit body or from ceiling tiles below the unit
7 Check condensate drain line – no overflow or standing water visible at drain outlet
8 Confirm return air grilles are not blocked by furniture, boxes, or other obstructions
9 Listen during operation – no abnormal noise (rattling, grinding, squealing, vibration)
C. INDOOR UNITS – WALL MOUNTED (FXAQ 20–50 PVE | IU-02 to IU-05, IU-16, IU-17, IU-19)
10 Visual inspection – no water leakage from unit body or along the wall below the unit
11 Check thermostat/remote display – no error codes or fault indicators displayed
12 Verify air inlet (front grille) and outlet (bottom louver) are clear and unobstructed
13 Listen during operation – no abnormal noise or vibration from unit
D. OUTDOOR UNITS – VRF CONDENSERS (RXYTQ 12/14/16 T7YF | VRFU-1-1 to VRFU-2-3)
14 Confirm all outdoor units are running – condenser fans rotating, no abnormal noise or vibration
15 Confirm no visible refrigerant oil staining or frosting on pipework, stop valves, or unit casing
16 Ensure air inlet (sides/rear) and air discharge (top fan outlets) are not obstructed
17 Check unit casing panels – no loose, missing screws or rattling panels

VRF SYSTEM – PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
WEEKLY PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
A. INDOOR UNITS – CEILING CONCEALED (FXSQ Series)
1 Inspect air filter condition through suction grille – note dust loading; clean if visibly blocked or restricted
2 Check condensate drain pump operation (where fitted) – confirm audible running and no water backup
3 Inspect condensate drain outlet – confirm free flow, no slime or algae buildup at drain tundish or piping
4 Check for frost/ice formation on refrigerant piping near indoor unit – sign of low charge or airflow blockage
5 Confirm indoor fan running smoothly – no wobble, hunting, or unusual airflow restriction
6 Verify supply air temperature at discharge diffuser is reasonable for current operating mode and setpoint
B. INDOOR UNITS – WALL MOUNTED (FXAQ Series)
7 Inspect air filter condition behind front grille – remove and check for dust buildup; clean if needed
8 Check drain drip tray and drain hose outlet – no overflow, no staining or watermarks on wall surface
9 Check for frost/ice on suction piping near unit – indicates possible airflow or refrigerant issue
10 Verify horizontal air louver auto-swing movement – no sticking or incomplete range of motion
C. OUTDOOR UNITS (RXYTQ-TYF | VRFU-1 & VRFU-2)
11 Inspect condenser coil fins – no blockage from dust, leaves, sand, or debris accumulation
12 Check condenser fan blades – no debris wrapping, no physical damage; fan guard intact and secure
13 Inspect unit base tray and drain holes – confirm no standing water accumulation inside base
14 Check clearance around all outdoor units – minimum 500 mm on each side should be maintained
15 Inspect unit casing for corrosion, surface damage, or loose panel fasteners
D. REF-NET PIPING & REFRIGERANT LINES
16 Visual inspection of all accessible refrigerant copper pipes – no frost, sweating, or oily staining at joints
17 Check pipe insulation (Armaflex or equivalent) – no tears, gaps, peeling, or moisture ingress signs
18 Inspect Ref-Net Y-joints (KHRQ 22M series) – no visible leakage, oil staining, or physical damage
E. CONTROLS & CENTRAL MANAGEMENT
19 Check DCM 601 A51 central controller – review operation log; note any recurring faults or zone lockouts
20 Spot-check 2-3 individual BRC1H 81W thermostats – verify setpoint vs room temperature reading within ±2°C
21 Verify communication between indoor units and central controller – all units visible and active in system map

VRF SYSTEM – PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
3-MONTH PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
A. INDOOR UNITS – CEILING CONCEALED (FXSQ 20A–125A) — Comprehensive Service
1 Remove and clean air filter(s) – wash with warm water (max 50°C), allow to fully dry before reinstalling
2 Inspect heat exchanger coil fins – clean with soft brush or low-pressure compressed air; note fouling level and fin damage
3 Clean condensate drain pan thoroughly – flush to remove algae, slime, and debris; apply biocide treatment if required
4 Perform drain flush test – pour water into drain pan and confirm free flow through drain line to discharge point
5 Test condensate drain pump (where fitted) – activate manually, clean float switch, confirm correct pump lift
6 Inspect electrical terminal block (power and signal cables) – tighten loose terminals; check for discolouration or overheating signs
7 Measure and record supply air temperature (dry bulb) at diffuser in cooling mode
8 Measure and record indoor unit current draw – compare to nameplate rating; flag any significant deviation
9 Verify refrigerant pipe connections at indoor unit – no frost, oil staining, or signs of refrigerant leakage
10 Check unit suspension bolts and ceiling brackets – confirm secure, no corrosion or looseness
11 Inspect all access panels and service openings – confirm gaskets intact and panels close properly
B. INDOOR UNITS – WALL MOUNTED (FXAQ 20–50 PVE) — Comprehensive Service
12 Remove and clean air filter(s) – wash with warm water, fully dry before reinstalling
13 Inspect and wipe heat exchanger fins with soft brush – note fin condition and any bending; straighten if needed
14 Clean drain drip tray – flush and confirm free drainage through drain hose to discharge point
15 Check wall mounting bracket – confirm secure and level; check for corrosion or cracking at fixing points
16 Inspect electrical connections at terminal block – tighten terminals, check cable insulation condition
17 Test horizontal louver auto-swing function – confirm full range of motion without sticking
18 Measure supply air temperature and compare with current setpoint – within ±2°C is acceptable
C. OUTDOOR UNITS (RXYTQ 12/14/16 T7YF | VRFU-1-1 to VRFU-2-3) — Comprehensive Service
19 Clean condenser coil fins – use soft brush or compressed air (inside-to-outside direction); inspect for bent or damaged fins
20 Check condenser fan blade condition – no cracks, bending, or debris; confirm fan guard is secure and undamaged
21 Measure condenser fan motor current – compare to nameplate rating; flag values outside acceptable range
22 Inspect electrical control box – check all power and control terminals, contactors, and wiring for overheating or corrosion
23 Check high-pressure and low-pressure switch wiring connections – confirm secure and no chafing
24 Inspect gas and liquid stop valves – confirm both fully open; check valve packing for refrigerant leakage signs
25 Check service port caps on all stop valves – confirm finger-tight and intact to prevent refrigerant loss
26 Check outdoor unit isolation pads and mounting bolts – no looseness, cracking, or significant corrosion
27 Clean debris from unit base drain tray and unit base frame – ensure drain holes are clear
28 Inspect unit casing – no significant corrosion, panel damage, or missing fasteners
D. REFRIGERANT SYSTEM – PRESSURE & LEAK INSPECTION
29 Perform visual refrigerant leak inspection on all accessible piping, flare joints, brazed connections, and Ref-Net Y-joints
30 Check refrigerant suction pressure (Low Side) at outdoor unit service port – record reading and compare to design value
31 Check refrigerant discharge pressure (High Side) at outdoor unit service port – record reading and compare to design value
32 Check subcooling and superheat values – confirm within Daikin VRV IV design parameters for current ambient conditions
E. REF-NET PIPING & INSULATION
33 Full visual inspection of all Ref-Net Y-joints (KHRQ 22M series) – no oil staining or signs of refrigerant leakage
34 Inspect copper pipe insulation (all sizes 6.4 mm to 43.3 mm OD) – repair all tears, gaps, and missing insulation sections
35 Check all pipe support hangers and clamps – no missing hardware; ensure no direct metal-to-metal pipe contact
F. CONTROLS & BMS
36 Verify DCM 601 A51 central controller settings – check zone schedules, group assignments, and operation mode setup
37 Check all BRC1H 81W thermostats for accuracy – compare room temperature reading against calibrated reference thermometer
38 Test automatic changeover function between cooling and heating mode across all zones
39 Review and clear accumulated fault log on DCM 601 A51 central controller – document any recurring error codes
40 Verify communication between indoor units and outdoor units – all units active with no communication fault errors

# CHECKPOINT OK ✓ NOT OK ✗ Remarks
VRF SYSTEM – PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
6-MONTH PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST
A. INDOOR UNITS – CEILING CONCEALED (FXSQ Series) — Full Overhaul Service
1 Complete all applicable 3-Month checklist tasks for ceiling concealed indoor units before proceeding
2 Deep clean heat exchanger coil with approved non-acidic coil cleaner solution (Daikin-approved product) – rinse thoroughly and dry
3 Inspect and clean blower/sirocco fan wheel – remove accumulated dust from all fan blades; check for imbalance
4 Check fan motor insulation resistance with megohmmeter – minimum 1 MΩ required; record result
5 Inspect PCB (printed circuit board) – check for discolouration, burnt components, moisture ingress, or pest damage
6 Check fan motor run capacitor condition – no bulging, cracking, or electrolyte leakage; replace if suspected faulty
7 Verify refrigerant pipe flare connections at indoor unit – confirm tightness (do not overtighten)
8 Conduct full condensate drain system test – simulate high-water condition to confirm drain pump activates correctly
9 Record unit operating data: supply air temp, return air temp, current draw – compare to commissioning baseline data
B. INDOOR UNITS – WALL MOUNTED (FXAQ Series) — Full Overhaul Service
10 Complete all applicable 3-Month checklist tasks for wall mounted indoor units before proceeding
11 Deep clean heat exchanger coil with approved coil cleaner – rinse thoroughly, ensure no chemical residue on fins
12 Check fan motor winding resistance – confirm no significant deviation from factory specification; record value
13 Inspect PCB assembly – no burning marks, moisture damage, or component failure; check connector pins for corrosion
14 Lubricate horizontal and vertical louver pivot pins if required – confirm full range of motion after servicing
15 Verify drain drip tray integrity – no cracks or gaps; confirm entire drainage path is clear and unobstructed
C. OUTDOOR UNITS (RXYTQ T7YF | VRFU-1 & VRFU-2) — Full Overhaul Service
16 Complete all applicable 3-Month checklist tasks for outdoor units before proceeding
17 Deep clean condenser heat exchanger coil using approved coil cleaner solution – rinse from inside outward with clean water
18 Measure compressor phase currents (all 3 phases) for each outdoor unit – record and compare to nameplate FLA
19 Measure refrigerant subcooling at condenser outlet liquid line – confirm within Daikin VRV IV service manual target range
20 Measure refrigerant superheat at outdoor unit suction port – confirm within Daikin VRV IV service manual target range
21 Verify total refrigerant charge – cross-check system operating pressures against ambient conditions and expected design values
22 Test high-pressure safety switch: confirm trip point and auto-reset function per Daikin service procedure
23 Test low-pressure safety switch: confirm trip point and manual reset function per Daikin service procedure
24 Inspect all electrical contactors and relays – check contact face condition; replace if pitting exceeds acceptable wear
25 Tighten all electrical terminations in outdoor unit control box – torque to Daikin specification; check insulation condition
26 Inspect inverter PCB/control board – no overheating, burning, or component failure signs; check heat sink cleanliness
27 Verify crankcase heater operation (if fitted) – important before cooler seasons to prevent liquid refrigerant migration to compressor
28 Check and confirm earthing/grounding connections at outdoor units – continuity verified with test instrument
D. FULL REFRIGERANT SYSTEM PERFORMANCE TEST
29 Perform full electronic refrigerant leak test (calibrated detector) on all joints, Ref-Net Y-joints, flare connections, and service ports
30 Record high-side and low-side pressures under full load operation – compare against previous service log and commissioning data
31 Assess system EER (Energy Efficiency Ratio) / COP – compare to design parameters; flag significant reduction for investigation
32 Verify Daikin VRV IV oil return cycle operation – confirm cycle runs without triggering fault alarms during test period
33 Confirm total refrigerant charge documentation: factory charge + additional field charge as recorded on unit nameplate service label
E. REF-NET PIPING — Thorough Inspection & Documentation
34 Sweep all Ref-Net Y-joints (KHRQ 22M series) with electronic refrigerant leak detector – document results for each joint
35 Inspect all copper refrigerant pipes (6.4 mm to 43.3 mm OD) – confirm full insulation coverage; repair all gaps without exception
36 Check all pipe support hangers and clamps – tighten as needed; ensure no vibration transfer to building structure
37 Verify all refrigerant pipe penetrations through walls/slabs – confirm fire-stopping and sealing remains fully intact
F. CONTROLS & BMS — Full Verification
38 Perform full functional test of DCM 601 A51 central controller – all zones respond, all schedules confirmed active
39 Calibrate each BRC1H 81W thermostat against NIST-traceable reference thermometer – adjust offset if deviation exceeds ±1°C
40 Test group mode changeover (cooling to heating and back) simultaneously for all VRF groups – confirm no zone lockouts
41 Review full 6-month fault history log on DCM 601 A51 – document all recurring faults and plan corrective actions
42 Verify BMS integration (if applicable) – confirm all data points are transmitting and logging correctly
43 Check for available firmware updates for DCM 601 A51 central controller – update if manufacturer-recommended
G. SERVICE DOCUMENTATION & HANDOVER
45 Update individual equipment history records with service date, findings, measurements, and all actions taken
46 Issue written recommendations for any upcoming repairs, spare parts requirements, or refrigerant top-up needs
47 Confirm all safety guards, access panels, grilles, and covers have been correctly reinstalled before handover
